deferred_source_units.reason: The general end, understanding and David heading is preserved; its common attribution alone does not establish a particular additional connection.

The loved words are expressly words of drowning, joined to a deceitful tongue. No specific counterpart is established without replacing that unusual supplied object with a more familiar destruction wording.
The promise of lasting thanks because God acted, and waiting for His kind name before the holy ones, remains unassigned rather than matched through generic praise alone.
The end, among hymns, understanding and David heading remains intact; no particular occasion or distinctive additional heading relation is established.
The paired appeal to salvation by God's name and judgment by His power is preserved; a general appeal to divine salvation does not suffice for an additional match.
Hearing prayer and giving ear to the speaker's mouth are preserved as prayer language without attaching a generic hearing petition elsewhere for credit.
God's help and support of the speaker's soul are preserved; no additional particular correspondence beyond this common confession of support has been established.
The common end, among hymns, understanding and David heading is retained without a separate connection based only on attribution.
The request that God hear prayer and not overlook the petition remains pending rather than linked merely through the ordinary prayer formula.
The command to attend and hear, followed by grief in meditation and trouble continuing into the next unit, is preserved without supplying an unexpressed subject or episode.
The enemy's voice, sinner's affliction, lawlessness turned upon the speaker and hostile anger remain a distinct continuation; no named persecutor is established.
The troubled heart and dread of death are preserved; a generic similarity to another frightened person would not establish a sufficiently particular connection.
The wording it will circle it upon its walls is retained with its unresolved pronouns. Lawlessness, toil and injustice in the city are not converted into a claim about identifiable enemy watchmen.
The counterfactual ability to endure an enemy's reproach or hide from a hater is preserved within the intimate-betrayal complaint; it does not establish a named betrayer for this unit.
The speaker's cry and the Lord's hearing remain unassigned because that general answer-to-prayer formula alone does not establish a particular additional match.
The future redemption of the soul in peace is followed by among many they were with me. That clause is not changed to many were against me, and no particular company is identified.

The heading expressly says foreigners seized David in Gath. The read Samuel account supplies David's arrival, fear and altered behavior there, but does not clearly establish the same seizure; the proposed episode remains a zero-credit candidate.
The enemies detested the speaker's words and thought evil against him. Detested is not replaced with twisted, and no more particular comparison of the actual wording is established.

The positive statement for nothing Thou wilt save them is preserved beside the future statement that in anger Thou wilt bring down peoples. Neither future declaration is negated or converted into an imperative to fit a familiar alternative reading.
Praise of an utterance in God and a word in the Lord is preserved without assigning an unstated possessor to the utterance or claiming that this unit explicitly says God's word.

The Saul-and-cave heading does not name the cave. Adullam after flight from Gath and the cave encounter while Saul pursued David are separately read possibilities, but neither is established as the heading's unique occasion.
The resolve to cry to God Most High, who has done good to the speaker, remains pending because no more particular target than general prayer and gratitude is established.
Passing water, reduction to nothing and God's stretching His bow until they weaken are preserved. The bow clause is not replaced with the breaking or blunting of arrows.
The thorns understanding buckthorn and the clauses as though alive, as in anger remain with the predicted swallowing. No cooking-pot or fuel interpretation is supplied to manufacture a target match.
The request for removal from enemies and redemption from attackers remains pending without identifying a particular adversary or retaining a generic deliverance parallel.
God's mercy reaching the speaker first and showing what concerns enemies remain as stated; a common assurance of mercy does not establish a particular additional target.
The reason for not killing them is lest they forget my people. This is not reversed into lest my people forget, and the ensuing scattering is not assigned to an unproved historical lesson.
The source describes scattering in search of food and grumbling if not filled. The condition is not strengthened into permanent insatiability, and no specific counterpart is retained for this unit.

The heading's Joab and twelve thousand are preserved. Samuel names David with eighteen thousand at Gaimale, and Chronicles names Abessa with eighteen thousand in the Valley of Salts. Common campaign features do not resolve the differing agents, counts and locators into the same event.

God gave those fearing Him a sign to flee from the bow. Jeremiah's read warning and flight context does not yet establish a sufficiently particular match to that sign; neither a displayed banner nor a truth clause is imported into the source.
The end, among hymns and David heading is preserved without a substantive connection based solely on generic heading elements.
The petition for God to hear and attend to prayer remains pending rather than receiving credit for a general hearing-prayer formula.

God as hope and a tower of strength before the enemy is preserved. The read Proverbs candidate speaks of greatness of strength, the Lord's name and runners raised high, but does not contain the anticipated tower; that proposed tower match is unestablished.
The confession of salvation, glory, help and hope upon God remains pending; common hope language alone does not supply a sufficiently particular additional relation.

The source says God spoke once and these two things I heard. Elihu's speech about the Lord speaking once and at a second time through a dream is a read possibility, but the source's two heard things are not converted into two divine utterances.

The heading places David in the wilderness of Judea without naming one episode. Read Samuel wilderness narratives do not establish a unique occasion, and generic location resemblance earns no connection credit.
I was seen by Thee in the holy place is preserved as the supplied passive clause. It is not changed into I beheld Thee, and no counterpart based on that different action is retained.
God's mercy being better than lives and the speaker's praising lips remain intact; no particular comparison beyond a general superiority-of-divine-goodness theme is established.
